title: Money that stays in town
instructions: Read the article about a town that has its own money. Decide whether the statements (1–8) are true (T) or false (F) according to the text, or whether the information is not given (NG) in the text. There is an example (0) at the beginning.
instructionsHu: Olvasd el a cikket egy városról, amelynek saját pénze van. Döntsd el, hogy az állítások (1–8) a szöveg szerint igazak (T), hamisak (F), vagy nem derül ki (NG). A 0. a példa.

passage.title: Money that stays in town
passage.subtitle: How one English town created its own banknotes

blocks.text: If you go shopping in Ashbridge, a market town of 15,000 people in the north of England, you might get some unusual change. Next to normal coins and notes, many shops here also accept the Ashbridge Pound – the town's own money. The colourful notes show local heroes, old buildings and even the river, and they were designed by students from the town's art college.

The idea came from Martin Hale, who owns a small bookshop on the high street. 'In 2020, half the shops in the centre were empty,' he remembers. 'People did all their shopping online or at the big supermarket outside town, so their money left Ashbridge immediately.' A year later, together with a group of other shop owners, Martin started the Ashbridge Pound.

The system is simple. You can change normal pounds into Ashbridge Pounds at the town hall or at the library: one normal pound buys one Ashbridge Pound. You can then spend them in more than 120 local businesses, from cafés and hairdressers to the vet. However, you can't use them at the big supermarket or in chain stores. Since last year, people who work for the town council can also choose to get part of their salary in Ashbridge Pounds.

But why would anyone want money that only works in one town? 'Because when I pay with Ashbridge Pounds, I know that my money helps my neighbours,' explains Priya Sharma, 17, who works on Saturdays at a bakery. 'The bakery buys its flour from a farm nearby, the farmer gets his hair cut in town, and so on. The money keeps going round in Ashbridge.' Priya's school has even used the local money in its economics lessons.

Not everyone is a fan, though. Some older people find it confusing to carry two kinds of money, and a few shops stopped accepting the notes after the first year because too few customers used them. There are also worries about fake notes, although the Ashbridge Pound has special security features, such as a hidden picture that you can only see under UV light.

So, has it worked? Martin believes it has. Today, only four shops on the high street are empty, and around £300,000 in Ashbridge Pounds is in use. 'It isn't magic,' he says, 'but it makes people think about where they spend their money. That's the real change.'

example.prompt: Students from Ashbridge designed the notes.
example.explanation: Igaz: a szöveg szerint a színes bankjegyeket a város művészeti főiskolájának diákjai tervezték („designed by students from the town's art college”).
example.evidence: they were designed by students from the town's art college

items.prompt: Martin Hale started the Ashbridge Pound on his own.
items.explanation: Hamis: Martin nem egyedül indította el, hanem más bolttulajdonosokkal együtt („together with a group of other shop owners”). Az „on his own” jelentése: egyedül, segítség nélkül.
items.evidence: together with a group of other shop owners, Martin started the Ashbridge Pound

items.prompt: Before the Ashbridge Pound started, about half of the shops in the town centre were empty.
items.explanation: Igaz: Martin szerint 2020-ban a belvárosi üzletek fele üresen állt, az Ashbridge-font pedig egy évvel később („A year later”), 2021-ben indult – tehát előtte volt üres a boltok fele.
items.evidence: In 2020, half the shops in the centre were empty

items.prompt: For every normal pound, you get more than one Ashbridge Pound.
items.explanation: Hamis: az átváltás egy az egyhez – egy rendes font pontosan egy Ashbridge-fontot ér („one normal pound buys one Ashbridge Pound”), tehát nem kapsz többet.
items.evidence: one normal pound buys one Ashbridge Pound

items.prompt: Priya gets part of her pay from the bakery in Ashbridge Pounds.
items.explanation: Nem derül ki: a szöveg csak annyit mond, hogy Priya szombatonként egy pékségben dolgozik, és ő maga Ashbridge-fonttal fizet. Hogy miben kapja a bérét, nem tudjuk – fizetést Ashbridge-fontban csak a városi önkormányzat dolgozóinál említ a szöveg, ez a csapda.
items.evidence: who works on Saturdays at a bakery

items.prompt: The bakery gets its flour from a farm close to Ashbridge.
items.explanation: Igaz: a pékség egy közeli farmról veszi a lisztet („from a farm nearby”). A „nearby” jelentése: a közelben – ugyanaz, mint a „close to Ashbridge”.
items.evidence: The bakery buys its flour from a farm nearby

items.prompt: Some shops no longer accept the Ashbridge Pound.
items.explanation: Igaz: néhány üzlet az első év után már nem fogadta el a helyi bankjegyeket, mert túl kevés vásárló használta őket („stopped accepting the notes”). A „no longer accept” = már nem fogad el.
items.evidence: a few shops stopped accepting the notes after the first year

items.prompt: People have already found fake Ashbridge Pound notes.
items.explanation: Nem derül ki: a szöveg csak azt mondja, hogy aggódnak a hamis bankjegyek miatt („worries about fake notes”), és hogy a bankjegyeken biztonsági elemek vannak. Azt nem írja, hogy találtak-e már hamisítványt.
items.evidence: There are also worries about fake notes

items.prompt: Today, there are no empty shops on the high street.
items.explanation: Hamis: ma is van négy üres üzlet a főutcán („only four shops on the high street are empty”). Az „only” azt jelzi, hogy ez kevés a korábbiakhoz képest, de nem nulla.
items.evidence: only four shops on the high street are empty
